newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad to get rate rise soon - sources.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad to get rate rise soon - sources.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan utility Electricidad de Caracas can expect a tariff increase in April but the hike will be less than the 40 percent the company asked for, sources at the Ministry of Energy and Mines told Reuters.
"Technically the company has already got the rise, but now comes the political part that actually authorizes the increase," said the source who asked not to be identified.
The source said Electricidad had asked for an average 40 percent rise based on 25 percent for industrial users and 85 percent for residential users. "But that was a lot," he said.
Market analysts have expected an average rise of between 15 and 20 percent.
"The increase already approved by technicians will allow Electricidad to cover its needs and I don't think it will have any problems accepting it," said the source.
The source declined to specify the rise, but said it would reduce current cross-subsidization of residential rates by industrial users.
At the same time, the hike would reduce losses the company suffers among its residential clients to minus four percent from current losses of minus eight percent.
Despite newspaper reports Wednesday that rate rises across the sector would be approved within the next two weeks, the source said April 1 was a more likely date.
"The government wants to see first of all how themes such as the public sector wage increase and social security reforms are going," he said.

The government recently approved an average 75 percent wage increase for its 1.2 million public sector workers to compensate for years of inflation that have shrunk real wages to 30 percent of 1980 levels. Social security reform talks are still ongoing.
